- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct — apply downward drag or lagged mean reversion.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.33–0.67), model frequently overestimates volatility; smooth forecast curve and reduce amplitude.
- When sentiment turns negative after a peak, model often fails to recognize reversal — adjust forecast to reflect mean reversion toward prior 10–15 day average.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate upward trend in early periods (e.g., 2022-12-27) — apply downward bias if sentiment is weak or event context suggests cooling.
- If sentiment is positive but price history shows no recent uptrend, model may overfit upward momentum — reduce forecast slope or anchor to recent 7-day average.
- In absence of clear event context, model often assumes continuation of prior trend — if sentiment shifts, adjust forecast to reflect sentiment change, not just price history.
